subject: Control-plane certificate propagation & proxy-chaining — review and PoC plan
messages:
From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@nebulasys.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Control-plane proxy chaining & cert propagation (diagram + questions)

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for taking a look at our private deployment constraints. Attached are two artifacts: a high-level network diagram (nebulasys-network-diagram.vsdx) and a short write-up of how we currently envision control-plane certificate propagation through the proxy chain (nebulasys-controlplane-proxy-chaining-v1.pdf).

Key constraints on our side:
- Air-gapped on-prem sites must not pull certs directly from public ACME endpoints.
- Control-plane components are colocated on a management VLAN; data-plane inference nodes live on tenant VLANs behind an egress firewall.
- Nebula wants to avoid routing TLS termination through the public ingress; prefer mTLS between sidecars.

Questions for Redwood:
1) How do you recommend propagating control-plane certificates to on-prem proxies without exposing private keys?
2) Can Redwood support chained TLS (edge proxy -> control-plane proxy -> service sidecar) while keeping our rotation window <= 7 days?
3) What operational tooling would you expect for rollbacks if a rotation causes connectivity loss?

Would love to schedule a short architecture review this week with your network/security folks.

Thanks,
Alex Kim
Solutions Architect — Nebula Systems
Attachments: nebulasys-controlplane-proxy-chaining-v1.pdf (application/pdf), nebulasys-network-diagram.vsdx (application/vnd.visio)

Subject: Re: Control-plane proxy chaining & cert propagation (diagram + questions)

Alex — thanks for the artifacts, they were very helpful. Quick read-through and proposed next steps below. Please note I forwarded the diagrams to our infra team (Irene + Karthik) for technical validation.

Short answers first:
- We recommend a Vault-led distribution model for private deployments (HashiCorp Vault or customer KMS/HSM integration), with certs injected into a short-lived sidecar file store and never egressed to public PKI.
- Chained mTLS is supported in our runtime; the trick is controlling certificate lifetimes and ensuring zero-downtime rotation via two-phase rollover (present old + new cert during transition). Sub-7-day rotations are feasible but require automated orchestration for the sidecars and a preflight validation.
- For rollbacks, we maintain a fallback policy: on rotation failure, proxies keep a cached previous cert (grace window) and control-plane will mark the rollout for manual rollback with a single API call. We'll include a reversible runbook.

Proposed architecture review agenda (30–45m):
1) Walk the diagram and call out egress/firewall constraints (5m)
2) Vault/KMS integration options and cert distribution flow (10m)
3) Proxy chaining behavior and token exchange (10m)
4) Acceptance criteria and rollback runbook (10m)

Can you do Wed 10/21 10:00 AM PT? If not, propose two times.

Leaving technical details to Irene and Karthik below — they will dump their notes after the review.

—Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Control-plane proxy chaining & cert propagation (diagram + questions)

Team — quick technical readout before the sync. I reviewed Nebula's diagrams and sketched a pragmatic PoC approach. Major notes: 

- Cert distribution model: use a central Vault cluster in Nebula mgmt VPC with an agent in the control-plane subnet. Vault issues short-lived mTLS certs to the control-plane proxies and a separate role for data-plane sidecars. Keys never leave the host disk unencrypted.

- Sidecar pattern: ship a lightweight envoy-based mTLS sidecar (Redwood runtime adapter) that mounts certs from a read-only tmpfs path created by the Vault agent. The sidecar will expose loopback interface for the inference process. This avoids application-level cert handling.

- Rotation cadence & two-phase rollover: implement newCert + oldCert acceptance window. Sequence: 1) Vault mints new cert; 2) sidecar loads both certs; 3) control-plane verifies connectivity; 4) oldCert garbage-collected after N days. Ensure the grace window covers clock skew and propagation delays.

- Chaining considerations: the control-plane proxy needs to validate client certs from upstream edge proxy and present an identity to downsteam sidecars. Recommend short L7 identity tokens (JWT) for intra-plane authorization in addition to mTLS to avoid cert-bound identity coupling.

- Failure modes & rollback: preflight probe (small handshake-only request) after cert load; if > 5% p99 latency increase or > 2% failure rate observed across probes in 5m window, auto-mark rollout failure and trigger rollback job. Manual rollback should be a single API call to the control-plane which signals sidecars to rebind to oldCert.

Action items for PoC:
- Jordan: finalize acceptance criteria draft and share runbook stub (I can iterate).
- Karthik: validate firewall/NAT traversal for Nebula's on-prem NAT topology (esp. inbound control-plane callbacks).
- Lauren: define test harness (cert rotation simulation + chaos scenario).

I expect a 4–6 week PoC to cover Vault integration, sidecar adapter validation, and a harmless rotation exercise.

Irene Choi
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@nebulasys.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 12:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Control-plane proxy chaining & cert propagation (diagram + questions)

Appreciate the thoughtful review, Irene. That approach maps well to our security constraints. A few clarifications from Nebula side: 

- Nebula will provide a Vault cluster in the management plane (we'll manage high-availability and HSM-backed auto-unseal). We prefer Redwood to run the Vault agent and the sidecar adapter within the control-plane images for consistency.
- Regarding JWTs for intra-plane authorization: we can mint short-lived tokens bound to cert CNs; we'll need a token exchange design to avoid token replay across tenants.
- For NAT traversal: our on-prem sites will allow outbound connections to the mgmt VPC on 443 and 8200 (Vault). Inbound callbacks are blocked; control-plane must be able to reach back to sidecars over the existing long-lived websocket/control channel.

I've uploaded an updated diagram and a sample Vault role file to the shared drive: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1NeBuLa-EXAMPLE-diagram .

We can take the PoC timeline of 4–6 weeks. We'll volunteer a single non-prod site for the initial test.

Wed 10/21 10:00 AM PT works for me — see calendar invite.

—Alex

Subject: Re: Control-plane certificate propagation & proxy-chaining — review and PoC plan

Alex — meeting confirmed and invite accepted. Attached is a first-draft acceptance criteria + runbook stub (redwood-acceptance-criteria-runbook-draft.md). Highlights pulled from Irene's notes:
- PoC success criteria: successful issuance + rotation of certs to sidecar without traffic interruption for 72h; preflight probes must remain within baseline, and rollback must be tested and exercised.
- Security checks: keys never written to persistent disk; Vault auto-unseal verified; RBAC roles scoped per tenant.
- Ops: a single rollback API and health-check endpoint for automated gating.

Karthik — can you confirm NAT traversal details by EOD Monday? Lauren — please start a small test harness repo and sketch tests for rotation and simulated propagation delay.

I'll iterate the runbook and share a versioned link after the sync. Thanks all.

—Jordan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
